name: El Niño / La Niña
summary: Very strong El Niño: Oceanic Niño Index +2.46°C for Aug–Oct, still rising
state: NOAA's Oceanic Niño Index for August–October, the latest available on 13 Nov, was +2.46°C, far above the +1.5°C threshold for a strong event (NOAA CPC). The index rose from +1.80°C for June–August and +2.16°C for July–September, and has risen in every three-month period since early 2026. The next value, for September–November, is due in early December.
for_you: Strong El Niño years tend to bring drought to Australia, southern Africa and Indonesia and heavier rain to parts of the Americas, with knock-on effects for food prices.
why: ENSO reshapes global weather for a year at a time — droughts, floods, hurricanes and crop yields.
drivers: Pacific trade winds and ocean heat content.
